html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Set and follow data governance requirements: lawful rights, quality and fitness
  • Record lineage and provenance
  • Plan and run training and testing, including bias, security and interpretability tests
  • Find and manage issues that appear in training and testing
  • Document the work to validate results and show compliance

2III.B.1: Set and follow data-governance requirements

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Establish, so the depth is Apply. The course has 2 practice questions on this indicator.

Running case

Whose Data Is This?

  • Daniel Osei asks Veridex where its hiring tool's training data came from; the answer is vague
  • For the customer assistant, Helios will ground answers in its own support documents, which need lineage and quality checks
  • Mei Tanaka worries about tampering with the document store
  • You must set the data rules, the test plan and the records

Data Governance for AI: The Requirements

  • Data governance gives every dataset an owner, rules for use, quality checks, access control, retention and records
  • AI Act Article 10 names eight practices for high-risk training, validation and testing data: design choices, origin and collection, preparation, assumptions, availability and suitability, bias examination, bias mitigation and gaps
  • Even outside the AI Act, these are the governance questions an auditor asks
  • Data governance applies to training, validation and testing data alike

Exam tip: Data governance for AI is the same discipline as for any data, plus bias, representativeness and provenance.

Lawful Rights to Collect and Use Data

  • Source and purpose: where did the data come from, and what was the original purpose? (Article 10(2)(b))
  • Privacy: a lawful basis, notice, minimization, sensitive-data rules and transfer mechanisms (module 4)
  • IP and contract: licenses, website terms, scraping rules and rights reservations (module 5)
  • Third-party data: warranties that the provider had the right to supply it, and audit rights
  • Confidentiality: customer and employee data have contractual limits
  • Document the assessment before the data are used, not after

Exam tip: If lawful rights are unclear, quality and accuracy do not matter: do not use the data until the rights are settled.

Data Quality: The Five Checks

  • Accuracy: values match reality; labels are right
  • Completeness: required fields and labels are present
  • Consistency: the same thing means the same thing across sources
  • Timeliness: data are current enough for the use; stale data mislead
  • Validity: values are in allowed formats and ranges
  • AI Act Article 10 asks for data that are relevant, sufficiently representative, free of errors as far as possible and complete

Exam tip: Quality is judged against the purpose: data that are fine for reporting can be poor for training.

Quantity, Representativeness and Fit for Purpose

  • Enough data is judged per group and per condition, not just in total
  • Representative: the data reflect the people and settings of real use, including geographic, contextual, behavioral or functional conditions (Article 10(4))
  • Gaps mean the model may perform worse or unpredictably where data are thin
  • Stale or detached data that no longer match the deployment setting lower trustworthiness (NIST)
  • Fit for purpose: the data answer the question the model is meant to answer

Exam tip: A big dataset is not a representative dataset.

Data Integrity and Protection

  • Integrity: the data have not been altered by accident or attack since they were approved
  • Controls: access control, version control, checksums or hashes, secure pipelines and audit trails
  • Data poisoning: an attack that manipulates training data to change model behavior; the AI Act names it among threats to guard against (Article 15)
  • Quarantine new data until checked; sample and inspect labels
  • Helios: the support-document store gets change control and owner approval

Exam tip: Whoever can change the training data can change the model's behavior.

3III.B.2: Record the lineage and provenance of the data

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Establish, so the depth is Apply. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Lineage: Where Data Came From and What Happened to It

  • Lineage is the traceable path of data from source to model: every step, change, owner and version
  • Why: to reproduce results, find the cause of a problem, remove data on request, and prove compliance
  • Record at each step: who did it, when, what changed, and the version produced
  • Link each trained model to the exact dataset versions used
  • Lineage makes deletion and correction requests possible (module 4)

Exam tip: If you cannot trace which data trained the model, you cannot fix, delete or defend it.

Provenance: Origin, Rights and Trust

  • Provenance is the origin and history of data: who created it, how, when, and on what terms
  • Provenance record: source, collection method, date, license or consent basis, labeling process and any transformation
  • External data: ask the provider for documentation, warranties and audit rights; vague answers are a risk finding
  • Synthetic data: record the generator and the real data it was based on
  • Helios: Veridex must document its training-data provenance before the hiring tool is relied on

Exam tip: Provenance answers where the data came from and whether you may use it; lineage answers what happened to it afterward.

Tools and Documents for Lineage and Provenance Beyond the BoK

  • Data catalogs and metadata: describe each dataset, its owner and its tags
  • Data versioning: each dataset version is fixed and identifiable; models reference versions
  • Hashes and registries: detect unexpected changes
  • Experiment tracking: links data, code, settings and results
  • Datasheets for datasets: a short document stating a dataset's motivation, composition, collection process and recommended uses
  • Audit trails: who accessed or changed what

Exam tip: A datasheet is to a dataset what a model card is to a model.

4III.B.3: Plan and run training and testing

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Plan, so the depth is Apply. The course has 2 practice questions on this indicator.

Planning Training and Testing

  • Plan before you train: objectives, data splits, metrics and thresholds, test types, tools and environments
  • Roles and independence: who builds, who tests, and who signs off; independent review reduces internal bias (NIST MEASURE)
  • Acceptance criteria: what must be true to move to the next stage
  • Thresholds are set first (module 8) so results cannot move the goalposts
  • Record the plan and any changes to it

Exam tip: A test plan written after the results is a report, not a plan.

Data Splits, Overfitting and Leakage

  • Training data teach the model; validation data tune settings and choose between models; test data are held out for a final, unbiased check
  • Overfitting: the model memorizes training data and fails on new data
  • Leakage: information from the test data (or from the answer) gets into training, so results look better than they are
  • Split before preprocessing, and use time-based splits when data change over time
  • Never tune on the test set

Exam tip: A model that scores perfectly on its own training data tells you nothing about how it will perform.

The Test Types, From Units to Interpretability

  • Unit: individual components behave correctly
  • Integration: components, data pipelines and interfaces work together
  • Validation: the model meets the requirements for its intended use
  • Performance: accuracy, error rates, speed and stability
  • Security: resistance to attacks and leakage of data
  • Bias: outcomes are acceptable across groups
  • Interpretability: reasons can be given to users and overseers

Exam tip: Match the test to the risk: leakage is a security test, group differences are a bias test.

Bias Testing and Fairness Metrics Beyond the BoK

  • Test by group, including intersections (for example sex and age together)
  • Selection rate and impact ratio: the rate of selection by group, lower over higher (module 5)
  • Demographic parity: equal selection rates across groups
  • Equal opportunity: equal true-positive rates among people who qualify
  • Equalized odds: equal true- and false-positive rates
  • These cannot all be satisfied at once in most real settings, so choose by context and record why
  • NIST asks that fairness and bias be evaluated and results documented (MEASURE 2.11)

Exam tip: Removing the protected attribute does not make a model fair, because proxies remain.

Mitigating Bias: Before, During and After Training Beyond the BoK

  • Before training: collect more representative data, re-sample or re-weight, fix labels, remove proxies
  • During training: add fairness constraints or objectives
  • After training: adjust thresholds (where lawful), add human review, keep monitoring
  • Retest after each change and record the trade-offs with accuracy
  • Some adjustments by group can raise legal questions; involve legal before using them
  • Helios: the proxy features were removed and the model recalibrated; the ratio rose to 0.91

Exam tip: Fixing the data usually beats patching the outputs; the order of preference mirrors the risk hierarchy.

Security and Interpretability Testing

  • Adversarial testing: inputs built to cause mistakes, and prompts built to break rules (for language models)
  • Data poisoning checks: look for manipulated or suspicious training records
  • Privacy leakage tests: can the model reveal or reproduce training data or personal information?
  • Robustness tests: performance under noise, drift and unusual inputs
  • Interpretability tests: can overseers and users get reasons for outputs? Feature-importance and example-based methods help
  • The AI Act's accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirement names poisoning, adversarial examples and confidentiality attacks (Article 15)

Exam tip: Security testing asks whether the model can be attacked or made to leak; it is separate from accuracy testing.

5III.B.4: Find and manage issues and risks found in training and testing

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Identify, so the depth is Understand. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Common Issues in Training and Testing

  • Overfitting: great on training data, poor on new data: simplify, add data, regularize
  • Leakage: suspiciously high scores: fix the split and retest
  • Label errors: inconsistent labels: audit and relabel
  • Unrepresentative data: poor results for some groups: collect more, re-sample
  • Poisoning: odd records or behavior: quarantine and investigate
  • Unlawful or unclear rights: stop, quarantine and escalate

Exam tip: Read the symptom in the question, and pick the response that fits it.

Managing Issues: Log, Triage, Fix, Retest

  • Log every issue with its severity and owner
  • Triage: does it affect people, legality or safety? Those go up first
  • Find the root cause and fix: change data, features, model or process
  • Retest and record that the issue is closed; escalate what cannot be fixed
  • Stop criteria: unresolved high-severity issues block the next stage
  • If unlawfully obtained data are found, quarantine them, ask legal and privacy for a decision, and record whether the model must be retrained; the EDPB treats the consequences as case-specific (module 4)

Exam tip: Unresolved lawfulness questions are stop-the-line issues, not items for the backlog.

Risks of Pretrained, Generative and Third-Party Models

  • Inherited issues: a pretrained or foundation model brings its own bias, data rights and memorization risks
  • Fine-tuning can add new data issues and can weaken safety behaviors
  • Benchmark contamination: test items may have been in the model's training data, so scores look inflated
  • Retrieval data (as at Helios) need quality, rights and freshness controls
  • Vendor evidence: ask for test reports, data documentation and known limitations, and verify key claims with your own tests

Exam tip: Buying a model does not remove your duty to test it for your use case.

6III.B.5: Document the training and testing

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Document, so the depth is Apply. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Documenting Training and Testing

  • Why: to validate results, show compliance and manage risk; to let others reproduce the work
  • Data: sources, versions, splits, lineage and provenance
  • Training: methods, settings, experiments and tools
  • Testing: test plan, metrics and thresholds, results by group, issues found and fixed, and sign-offs
  • Decisions: why this model, this threshold and this trade-off were chosen
  • NIST asks that test sets, metrics and tool details used in TEVV be documented (MEASURE 2.1)

Exam tip: A result without its data version, settings and test set cannot be reproduced or defended.

Model Cards and Test Reports Beyond the BoK

  • A model card is a short document that accompanies a model: intended use, performance across groups, the conditions of evaluation, and limitations
  • It links to the datasheet for the training data
  • It supports deployers who need to know what the model can and cannot do
  • The AI Act's Annex IV asks for similar detail: data requirements, validation and testing with metrics, and discriminatory impacts
  • Helios: asks Veridex for a model card and checks it against its own test results

Exam tip: A model card tells users where the model works and where it does not, so state both.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (one best answer, or select exactly the number the question asks for)

S1Daniel Osei wants to use Helios's past support tickets to ground the customer assistant. Which check must come first?

  • ATuning the retrieval settings so that the assistant finds the best answers in the tickets quickly and reliably
  • BChecking the spelling and formatting of the tickets so that the text is clean and ready for the assistant
  • CConfirming Helios may use the tickets for this purpose, including personal data and confidentiality terms
  • DComparing the assistant's answers with those of a competitor's assistant to set a clear performance goal
Show the answer

Answer: C. Lawful rights come first: if Helios may not use the tickets for this purpose, quality and tuning do not matter. The ticket text contains personal data and may carry confidentiality terms, so the rights check has to happen before the data are used.

S2Which TWO checks assess the quality and fitness for purpose of data for a hiring screening model? (Select TWO.)

  • ACounting the graphics processors that are available for the training run
  • BChecking that the applicant data cover the groups and settings in which the model will be used
  • CReviewing which vendor offers the lowest price for storing the training data over several years
  • DMeasuring the rate of missing values and label errors in the training data
  • EMeasuring how quickly the data can be copied between two cloud regions
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Fitness for purpose depends on how representative the data are for the real population and setting, and on error and completeness rates in values and labels. Compute capacity, storage price and transfer speed are operational matters, not data quality.

S3A vendor cannot say where the data used to train its tool came from. What is the best governance response?

  • AAccept the tool, because vendors are not required to document anything about their training data sources
  • BRely on the vendor's reputation and its other customers as evidence that the data were obtained lawfully
  • CTest the accuracy of the tool, since the origin of the data does not affect what the tool can do for users
  • DTreat it as an open provenance risk: ask for documentation and warranties, and avoid high-risk reliance
Show the answer

Answer: D. Provenance determines whether the data may be used and what risks they carry, so missing documentation is a finding. The buyer should ask for documentation, warranties and audit rights, and avoid high-risk reliance until it is resolved.

S4Which practice best prevents data leakage when evaluating a model?

  • ASplitting the data before preprocessing and keeping the test set untouched until the final check
  • BUsing the test set repeatedly while tuning, so that the final model is optimized for it
  • CTraining on the available data first and then selecting a test sample from that same data pool
  • DReusing the validation data as the test data, so that fewer records are needed for evaluation
Show the answer

Answer: A. Leakage happens when information from the test data reaches training or tuning. Splitting first and leaving the test set untouched until the end keeps the final check unbiased. The other practices mix the sets and inflate results.

S5Helios will test the hiring tool for bias. Which TWO actions fit? (Select TWO.)

  • AEvaluating the overall accuracy, because it summarizes the performance of the tool
  • BRemoving the protected attribute and treating the tool as fair without further testing
  • CComparing selection rates and the impact ratio across groups, including intersections
  • DTesting on the training set, because the model has already learned from that data
  • EComparing error rates, such as true-positive rates, across groups among qualified applicants
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. Bias testing compares outcomes and errors across groups, including intersections. Overall accuracy can hide group gaps, removing an attribute leaves proxies, and testing on the training data says nothing about new applicants.

S6During training, a team learns that part of its dataset was scraped in breach of the source's terms. What is the best response?

  • AContinue training, because the data are already in the pipeline and the work is almost finished now
  • BQuarantine the data, escalate to legal and privacy, and decide with them on removal and retraining
  • CDelete the log entries about the source, so that the issue does not appear in the audit trail
  • DKeep the data but exclude the source's name from the dataset documentation to avoid questions
Show the answer

Answer: B. Data with unclear or breached rights are a stop-the-line issue: quarantine them, escalate, and decide on removal and retraining with legal and privacy input, recording the decision. Continuing, deleting records or hiding the source makes the risk worse.

S7Which content best belongs in a model card?

  • AThe marketing slogan, the price list and the sales contacts for the customers who buy the model
  • BThe full source code and the private keys that the model needs to run in the production system
  • CThe names of the individuals whose data were used to train the model, with their home addresses
  • DThe intended and out-of-scope uses, the evaluation data, performance by group, and known limits
Show the answer

Answer: D. A model card states what the model is for, how it was evaluated, how it performs across groups and where it falls short. Marketing material, secrets and personal data do not belong in it.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Data rules lawful rights first; then quality, representativeness and integrity; protect against tampering
Lineage and provenance trace data from source to model; record origin, rights and changes
Training and testing plan first; split data properly; unit to interpretability tests; test bias by group; mitigate before, during and after
Issues log, triage, fix, retest; stop on unresolved high severity or unclear rights
Records data, methods, metrics, results by group, decisions; datasheets and model cards
